label: Beginnings have a concrete ground present at the absence or later
definition: BeginningsHaveLastingGround h Concrete grounds holds when, in every history v, a concrete individual x that is not present at a moment s and is present at a strictly later moment t has some concrete individual y with grounds v y x that is present at s or at some moment strictly after s (in v). In ordinary language: whatever concrete thing begins to be present has a concrete ground whose presence is not wholly confined to times before the moment of its absence (it may first appear at or after that moment). A fire lit at noon, absent at dawn, whose match is present just before ignition satisfies it. Because it is existential, a remote ground that ceased long before s (a grandparent who died before s, of a child born after s) does not violate it, provided some ground (a parent) is present at s or later. It is violated by a beginning with no concrete ground at all, and by a beginning whose only grounds were present only before s and produced it across s (GroundedBeginnings.Control.ceased).
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred. Sense of ground (DISAMB-CAUSAL-SERIES): the relation is a supplied world-relative parameter of the shape of BruteFoundationBoundary.Profile.grounds; the intended reading for the warrant is the proximate ground of the thing's coming to be (the cause from which its coming to be takes its origin), per se or per accidens, not a remote ancestor; the derivation is valid for any relation. The ground need not be a sufficient or deterministic cause, and it need not exist in v: presence in v is given by the clause, existence only by the separate presence-to-existence premise A1. 'Concrete' is the supplied predicate of A2 (DISAMB-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CRITERIA). Merges two earlier formulations after the semantic challenge of PR #1478: 'every beginning has a concrete ground' (BeginningsGrounded, kept for the controls) and a universal 'no ground ceased before the absence', which ordinary remote grounds violate. Its presence clause bounds the ground's presence from below, ComingToBeHorns.GroundsPrecedeAt from above. Extension from ordinary beginnings to every possible history, including one with a wholly empty earlier moment, is an explicit OPEN bridge.
